Parent page (localhost:8765)

Serve this directory twice and open this page as http://localhost:8765/inline-icon-iframe-parent.html:

cd ChromeExtension/tests/fixtures && python3 -m http.server 8765
cd ChromeExtension/tests/fixtures && python3 -m http.server 8766

The frames below load from 127.0.0.1:8766, not localhost:8766. The differing port already makes them a separate origin, but that alone is not enough to test what this fixture exists to test: MyPass matches entries by hostname only, ignoring scheme and port, so a localhost frame inside a localhost parent would be offered an identical entry list and "the frame gets its own entries" could not fail. 127.0.0.1 is a different hostname from localhost, so the vault can hold a distinct entry for each and the difference is visible.

Set-up: save two entries in MyPass before starting — one for localhost and one for 127.0.0.1, with clearly different usernames. Every "the lists differ" expectation below depends on it.

1. Cross-origin login form

Expect: the key icon appears inside the frame; the entries it lists are the 127.0.0.1 ones and not this page's localhost ones; filling lands in the frame and leaves this page untouched.

2. Narrow frame — known limitation

Expect: the icon appears, but the panel is clipped by the frame's width. Recorded in the design, not a defect to file.

3. Cross-origin frame containing a 2FA setup link

Expect: nothing. The 2FA candidate scan and the "save 2FA" banner are top-frame work, so the otpauth link in this frame must produce no banner here and none on this page either, and the popup's Add 2FA section must not pick it up from inside the frame.

4. Ad-like frame

Expect: no errors. It holds no form and no body-level content worth touching — it is here so the "several third-party frames, no errors on chrome://extensions" check has something real to observe.

5. This page's own field

Expect: its own icon, filling with entries for localhost.

Also expect: no save-password and no save-2FA banner ever appears inside any frame, including after submitting the form inside frame 1 — banners belong to the top frame only, and they only ever fire on submit, so a frame that is never submitted proves nothing.
